name: Nahuatl
notes: STRUCTURAL ADSTRATE STUB (not a modelled G2P target). Nahuatl (Aztecan, Uto-Aztecan) is the principal indigenous adstrate of central and highland Mexican Spanish, with Nawat/Pipil in El Salvador. It exists so that the ancestry and phylogenetic-distance metrics of the Latin American Spanish varieties that reference it as an adstrate have a node to resolve to. It carries no grapheme table. Nahuatl spelling differs between varieties and conventions, so a table belongs to the spec of one variety, with a cited description of the orthography it uses. ISO 639-3 has no code for Nahuatl as a whole: each Nahuatl variety has its own individual code. The ISO 639-5 collective code for the Nahuatl languages is `nah`.

sources.author: Campbell, Lyle
sources.title: American Indian Languages: The Historical Linguistics of Native America
